title: WireGuard VPN troubleshooting — binary decision tree (client vs server; overlay-WAN vs remote-access)

n_role.instructions: Is the NSE acting as the WireGuard SERVER (listening for remote-access peers) for this scope, rather than as a WireGuard client?

criteria.true: show_config has a `vpn-server` section with `wireguard` / `wireguard-user` blocks — the NSE listens for remote peers
criteria.false: show_config configures the NSE as a WireGuard CLIENT: `interface vwan` (overlay-WAN) or `vpn-client wireguard`

n_vwan.instructions: Is this WireGuard client configured as an overlay / virtual-WAN interface?

criteria.false: a plain `vpn-client wireguard` client, not overlay-WAN

n_license.instructions: Is the overlay-wan feature license active on this device?

criteria.false: overlay-wan is absent or Disabled in show_feature_license (subscription missing/expired)

n_c_handshake.instructions: Does `wg show` report a recent `latest handshake` for the relay/peer with non-zero transfer?

criteria.true: wg show shows a recent 'latest handshake' AND non-zero transfer for the peer — the tunnel is up
criteria.false: the peer shows 'latest handshake: (never)' or has no handshake/endpoint — not establishing

n_c_udp.instructions: Is the client sending handshake initiations but receiving no reply (outbound UDP to the relay blocked)?

criteria.true: wg show shows handshakes never completing with transfer 'X sent, 0 received' — initiations leave, nothing returns

n_c_timeskew.instructions: Is the NSE clock materially skewed, causing handshakes to be rejected as stale?

criteria.true: the NSE date/time is >5 min off real time, or logs show 'stale handshake' / 'replay' rejections

n_c_keepalive.instructions: Is connectivity intermittent with rapidly cycling handshakes (CGNAT closing the UDP mapping because PersistentKeepalive is too long)?

criteria.true: handshakes succeed then drop within seconds-to-minutes of idle; keepalive at/above 25s on a CGNAT carrier

n_c_mtu.instructions: Tunnel is healthy but large packets fail (small pings ok, large ping -s1400 / SIP / large transfers fail)?

criteria.true: recent handshakes + counters ticking, but large packets are lost while small ones succeed (MTU/fragmentation)

n_s_handshake.instructions: Does `wg show` report a recent `latest handshake` for the affected user/peer with counters ticking?

criteria.true: recent handshake + transfer for the peer — control-plane is up
criteria.false: the peer shows 'latest handshake: (never)' — never connected

n_s_inbound_permit.instructions: Does the firewall config include an inbound WAN permit for the WireGuard listen port?

criteria.true: show_config / nft has an inbound permit for UDP <wg listen port> on the WAN — packets can reach the server, so a no-handshake is a config/key mismatch
criteria.false: no inbound permit for the WG port on the WAN — inbound UDP is blocked

n_s_allowedips.instructions: Do the user's AllowedIPs / allowed-subnets NOT include the LAN subnet the client is trying to reach (or the route isn't installed)?

criteria.true: the configured allowed-subnets / AllowedIPs for this peer omit the destination subnet, or no wg route is installed for it
criteria.false: AllowedIPs includes the destination and the route is installed

n_s_peruser.instructions: Does this user have a per-user allowed-subnets whitelist that EXCLUDES the destination (works for another user with broader access)?

criteria.true: a per-user allowed-subnets list is set and the destination is not in it (whitelist-only, not additive)
criteria.false: no restrictive per-user list, or the destination is included

n_s_snat.instructions: Is there asymmetric reachability with an internally-inconsistent SNAT config on the WG tunnel (masquerade without a matching exempt/ACL, or SNAT contradicting stated intent)?

criteria.true: a SNAT rule masquerades the source but the destination has no corresponding exempt/permit, causing asymmetric reachability (a genuine SNAT problem)
criteria.false: SNAT config is consistent, or no SNAT is involved

n_s_mtu.instructions: Do large packets fail, or is the clock skewed (MTU/PMTU or time-skew on the remote-access tunnel)?

criteria.true: large packets lost while small succeed (MTU), or the NSE clock is materially skewed (handshake time validation)
criteria.false: no size-dependent loss and the clock is correct

leaf_client_establish_unknown.note: Client tunnel not establishing but no A2/A5/A3 signature matched — run the Case A differential (subscription, outbound-UDP reachability, keepalive, MTU, time skew) manually with bilateral evidence.

leaf_client_healthy.note: Client tunnel is up with no MTU issue — the problem is post-WG (routing/NAT/firewall). Run the differential; see vpn-tunnel-up-lan-hosts-unreachable.

A1.title: Security Plus subscription missing or expired
A1.mechanism: Overlay WAN over CGNAT is a Security Plus feature; when the subscription lapses the relay control plane stops accepting the NSE and the WireGuard tunnel never establishes.
A1.fix: Renew/upgrade the device's Security Plus subscription via cnMaestro X. Short-term: fall back to IPsec S2S if one end has a public IP.

A2.title: Outbound UDP to the overlay relay blocked
A2.mechanism: The overlay tunnel runs outbound from the NSE to Cambium's relay over UDP; some carriers (CGNAT cellular, corporate upstreams) block outbound UDP or specific port ranges.
A2.fix: Verify the relay endpoint is reachable; check the carrier for outbound-UDP/port blocking; if a port range is blocked switch the WireGuard port (UDP 443 emulation if available); escalate to the carrier if policy-enforced.

A3.title: NAT keepalive interval too long (CGNAT mapping closed)
A3.mechanism: CGNAT UDP mappings time out aggressively; if PersistentKeepalive is longer than the carrier's UDP timeout the mapping closes between keepalives and the tunnel goes dark until the next one.
A3.fix: Lower PersistentKeepalive to 10-15s on the overlay-wan config to survive aggressive CGNAT UDP timeouts.

A4.title: MTU / fragmentation over the overlay path
A4.mechanism: WireGuard adds ~60 bytes; over constrained paths the effective overlay MTU drops below 1500 and large packets fragment or are silently dropped.
A4.fix: Lower the WireGuard interface MTU (try 1380, or 1280 over CGNAT/cellular) and enable TCP MSS clamping.

A5.title: Time skew breaks handshake validation
A5.mechanism: WireGuard handshakes carry a timestamp; a materially skewed NSE clock makes the relay reject every handshake as stale.
A5.fix: Force NTP sync immediately; verify NTP servers are reachable; configure multiple NTP servers on a path the tunnel doesn't depend on.

B1.title: Client config doesn't match NSE-side config
B1.mechanism: Mismatched PublicKey, wrong Endpoint host:port, or non-overlapping AllowedIPs mean the tunnel never establishes for that user.
B1.fix: Re-issue the user's config from the NSE (cnMaestro → Remote VPN → WireGuard → user → Generate Config) and have them re-import; verify Endpoint host:port matches the NSE WAN IP + listen port; compare PublicKey byte-for-byte.

B2.title: Inbound UDP blocked at the NSE WAN
B2.mechanism: WireGuard listens on UDP; if the WAN firewall has no inbound permit for the listen port, a Geo-IP rule filters the source, or the ISP drops unsolicited inbound UDP, the client never reaches the server.
B2.fix: Add an inbound WAN permit for UDP <wireguard_port>; check the Geo-IP allow list for the client's country; if the upstream ISP blocks unsolicited inbound UDP, use Overlay WAN (Case A) instead.

B3.title: AllowedIPs / install-routes missing or wrong
B3.mechanism: AllowedIPs is both the cryptokey routing table and the route-install hint; if the NSE side omits the LAN subnets the client wants, traffic is received-but-not-routed.
B3.fix: In cnMaestro add the LAN subnets to the user's Allowed Subnets; update the client-side [Peer] AllowedIPs to include the NSE LAN subnets; verify the route is installed in the main table.

B4.title: SNAT intent mismatch (THE CANONICAL FIXATION CASE)
B4.mechanism: Some deployments intentionally SNAT WG-tunnel traffic to the NSE address for simpler LAN-side routing; others expect transparency. The agent must NOT assume SNAT should be removed.
B4.fix: CLARIFY the intended NAT behavior FIRST. If SNAT wanted: verify exempt entries cover the right (src,dst) pairs and fire before WAN-masquerade. If transparent wanted: add the SNAT exempt for <LAN_subnet>.<client_subnet> AND ensure LAN devices route the client subnet via the NSE.

B5.title: Per-user restrictions blocking expected access
B5.mechanism: A per-user allowed-subnets list is whitelist-only (not additive to a global default); traffic to any subnet not in the list is silently dropped.
B5.fix: Update the user's allowed-subnets in cnMaestro to include the required destination subnet (confirm intent to broaden access).

B6.title: Tunnel UP, counters ticking, but specific destinations unreachable
B6.mechanism: WireGuard is healthy but a specific destination is unreachable — same post-decrypt forward-chain failure class as IPsec.
B6.fix: Defer to the vpn-tunnel-up-lan-hosts-unreachable playbook (ACL deny, table-220 leak, geo-IP RFC1918 drop, SNAT exempt missing, ARP unreachable, post-FORWARD drop).

B7.title: Time skew or PMTU (mirrors A4 and A5)
B7.mechanism: MTU/fragmentation and handshake-time-validation apply identically to remote-access WireGuard.
B7.fix: MTU: lower the WG interface MTU / enable MSS clamping (see A4). Time skew: force NTP sync (see A5).
